recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Reintroducing the intermediate 2018 at-least-one wording would be less accurate than the current request/response rule, and no follow-up FHIR core edit is needed for this seed.
issue_request: FHIR-17076 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 FHIR-core HTTP issue asking to replace wording that said each history Bundle entry SHALL minimally contain either a resource or a request with entry.request.method, because either/or implied an exclusive-or even though entries may contain both.
initial_application: SVN revision 14177, represented by git commit 5f6a350dc60ebe7f93c6bb90dbcba4fde0a56ba8, applied the issue by changing source/http.html from 'either a resource' to 'at least one of: a resource' in the history interaction paragraph.
additional_context: The same current HTTP history paragraph was later reconciled under FHIR-7933 by existing combined-branch commit 2923d2b222a056456cf57b6951980621825b7e7f, which replaced the old at-least-one sentence with current wording requiring request and response elements and requiring a resource for PUT/POST history entries while omitting it for DELETE. A 2018 implementers Zulip thread on the old sentence supports the DELETE/resource interpretation and did not reveal conflicting guidance.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Current source/http.html no longer contains the misleading either/or wording, and a source-wide search found no remaining occurrence of the old phrase in active source.

related_jiras.note: An existing combined-branch reconciliation changed the same HTTP history paragraph to the current request/response wording, preserving the non-XOR interpretation while superseding the older at-least-one sentence.
